core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 8909-8914): take a K-injective complex I^bullet representing M and a K-flat complex L^bullet representing L.

Identify the complexes (proof lines 8915-8927): for any complex K^bullet the composition lemma gives the displayed identity between SheafHom(K^bullet, SheafHom(L^bullet, I^bullet)) and SheafHom(Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet), I^bullet).

Conclude (proof lines 8928-8931): the left-hand side represents the derived internal hom into the derived internal hom (by the flat-into-injective lemma) and the right-hand side represents the derived internal hom from the derived tensor product, which gives the displayed isomorphism; taking global sections and using the identification of H^0 with derived Hom recovers the chapter's equation for internal homs.
proof_roadmap: Resolve the two arguments by a K-injective and a K-flat complex.
Use the composition lemma for internal homs to identify the two complexes termwise.
Read off the derived statement and the global sections formula.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the adjunction-style identity between the internal hom into an internal hom and the internal hom from the derived tensor product (statement lines 8895-8906). The proof (proof lines 8908-8931) chooses a K-injective and a K-flat representative, applies the composition lemma for internal homs, and identifies both sides through the flat-into-injective lemma and the description of H^0 of the internal hom as derived Hom. H2: one choice of representatives plus one identification, written out.
